source_hypotheses.required: The exact incoming assertions listed in this join.
source_hypotheses.constructed: For the actual D210 family, choose finite L-defined B-linear mu_sigma with mu_1=1. Their rational central discrepancies satisfy the cocycle identity; Tate functoriality holds for every ell. For rational discrepancy c, degree on rational quasi-isogenies and positive fourth roots give epsilon=c/|c|. No finite splitting is claimed by this result. For constant root-of-unity modules, the local character square-root obstruction over Q_p is determined by chi(-1). For an inflated normalized sign cocycle and the stated L,T, construct finite continuous cochain eta valued in mu_(2m), eta squared=chi and delta eta=epsilon. The product order bound is generic; later numerical estimates remain separate. The cochain restricts to a conjugacy-invariant character on G_L. Quadratic modification removes outside-T inertia without changing square or coboundary; its kernel field has degree at most2m[L:Q].
source_hypotheses.justification: C2 constructs b with b squared=chi and delta b=epsilon. C3 preserves both identities under the outside-T quadratic adjustment and defines the same L-prime as the kernel on G_L. Thus (b_sigma inverse nu_sigma sigma)(b_tau inverse nu_tau tau) equals b_sigma_tau inverse nu_sigma_tau sigma_tau, because epsilon/(b_sigma b_tau)=1/b_sigma_tau. B-linearity gives commutation. On G_L-prime the inflated mu is1, a=1 and b=1, giving the actual Tate restriction. Original matrix units then give rho_ell=r_ell direct-sum r_ell. This proof uses no compatibility or irreducibility conclusion.
